Compute TF module enrichment using directed target genes

compute.modules.enrichment.Rd

This function performs enrichment analysis for transcription factor (TF) modules using known TF-target interactions. For each module, it takes the hub TFs and retrieves their known targets from the TF-target network (CollecTRI by default). It then conducts an over-representation analysis (ORA) against the Reactome pathway database. To reduce redundancy, only unique pathways per module are retained by filtering out overlaps between modules.

Usage

compute.modules.enrichment(
  counts_norm,
  hub_tfs,
  TF.collection = "CollecTRI",
  universe = NULL,
  cancer_type = NULL,
  top_n = 10,
  file_name = NULL
)

Arguments

counts_norm

A numeric matrix of normalized gene expression values. Rows are gene symbols, columns are samples. This matrix is used to restrict the universe of genes used in enrichment and validate TF-target gene presence.

hub_tfs

A list of hub TFs per module, typically obtained using identify_hub_TFs(). This should be a list of two elements: one with named hub TFs per module, and another with their module membership or additional metadata. Only the modules in this list (those with hub TFs) are analysed.

TF.collection

Character. The TF-target network from which the targets of the hub TFs are taken: "CollecTRI" (default), "Dorothea" (confidence A and B) or "ARACNE", read as in compute.TFs.activity(). Use the collection the TF activity was computed with.

universe

Optional. A user-specified data frame of TF-target interactions (columns source and target), used instead of TF.collection.

cancer_type

Optional character. Cancer type used to locate the ARACNe network (input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt), only used when TF.collection = "ARACNE". If NULL, the network is auto-detected when only one exists under input/ARACNE/.

top_n

Integer. Number of pathways shown in the dot plot of each module. Default is 10. All the pathways are in the returned tables.

file_name

Optional character suffix for the names of the saved plots.

Value

Invisibly, a list with two elements, each a named list with one table per module (the result table of ReactomePA::enrichPathway(), or NULL for a module without enrichment):

  • enrichment: the module-specific pathways (adjusted p-value < 0.05, and not significant in any other module).

  • enrichment_all: all the significant pathways of each module, before removing those shared between modules.

For each module with module-specific pathways, a dot plot is also saved in the Results/ directory as a PDF file named Enrichment_Reactome_Module_<color>_<file_name>.pdf (Enrichment_Reactome_Module_<color>.pdf without file_name). If no enrichment is found for a module, a message is given and no file is saved for that module. An error is raised if none of the hub TFs is in the TF-target network, or if none of their targets is found in the row names of counts_norm (they must be gene symbols).

Details

The targets of the hub TFs are taken from the TF-target network (for CollecTRI and Dorothea, cached in Results/TF_target_collection_<TF.collection>.csv), and ReactomePA::enrichPathway() is used for ORA with the Reactome database. The ORA input is the 20% most variable targets of the module's hub TFs; a module with fewer than 5 such genes is skipped with a message. The background is all the genes of counts_norm. Any set of TFs has targets enriched in the pathways those TFs regulate, so the results describe what the hub TFs of each module regulate, not evidence that the module itself is special. Pathways enriched in more than one module are removed, so only module-specific results are kept. TF names are matched in their syntactic form too (e.g. NKX2.1, as returned by compute.TFs.activity(), matches NKX2-1).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Identify the hub TFs of a TF network from compute.WTCNA()
hub_tfs <- identify_hub_TFs(wgcna_network, mm_thresh = 0.8, degree_thresh = 0.9)

# Perform module-level Reactome enrichment
enr <- compute.modules.enrichment(counts.norm, hub_tfs)
head(enr$enrichment[[1]])
} # }
